antiBubbleFloor.counts: completed new cards only, rebuilt from history (permitted inputs, no served log is stored): a card counts as moved if it was not the first eligible card of the default order when it was completed. Learner-chosen cards (map, search) and pre-personalisation history count as moved, so a first session usually starts on the default card. Cards left before the reveal and due revisits do not count. Past items are judged against today's default order and filter, so a catalog change can shift the count.
antiBubbleFloor.knownGap: skipped moved cards do not count (sim: max 4 moved served in a row vs 2 completed)

objective.primary: mean simulated first spaced-revisit recall over ALL lessons completed (not only moved ones)
guardrails: share of completed new cards in the learner's top domain does not rise vs default-order (breadth)
distinct concepts completed does not fall vs default-order (breadth within a domain)
share of cards shown before their prerequisites does not rise

why.base: guess: same as COMPOSER.weights.defaultRank (1.0), so the default order is the base and a departure must earn its place
why.onRem.repair: guess: same as COMPOSER.weights.onRem.repair, so v1 differs from gam only by the session machinery
why.onRem.build: guess: same as COMPOSER.weights.onRem.build, so v1 differs from gam only by the session machinery
why.onRem.breadth: guess: same as COMPOSER.weights.onRem.breadth, so v1 differs from gam only by the session machinery
why.onRem.stretch: guess: same as COMPOSER.weights.onRem.stretch, so v1 differs from gam only by the session machinery
why.onCov.repair: guess: mild overlap: a second repair card on a need the session already covered adds less; EDP v1 gives every primary need a negative on_cov
why.onCov.build: guess: mildest overlap: build addr is fixed from history for the session, so a second build card is another successor of a recalled concept (a parallel frontier step), not a repeat; the penalty is small
why.onCov.breadth: guess: strong overlap: one card from another domain meets breadth for a session; more is a switch, not breadth
why.onCov.stretch: guess: strong overlap: one stretch card per session (O8: stretch before readiness is the riskiest move)
why.slotDecay: guess: .01 (model-v0.4.1; was .02). A departure needs +.01 more per slot (+.04 by session slot 4), because later slots rest on assumed coverage, not evidence (O2). Scaled from EDP: its need widgets' slot_decay averages .058 and its default widgets' .035, a .023 per-slot differential against a median primary on_rem of 1.75, i.e. .013 per unit of need mass; ours in the same units is slotDecay / onRem (mean .39), so EDP's own differential would be .005. .01 keeps a 2x O2 premium (it was 4x). It no longer ends a v3 chain by itself: with the synergy at .7 x onRem a follow-on card clears the score bar through slot 4, and EDP's own stopping rule ends the chain, the attention budget (the follow-on must still resolve more than attentionCost of need mass; gam-session-params.md)
why.attentionCost: guess: .06 (model-v0.4.1; was .1), EDP's cost (edp-engine.js compose, cost=.06). From model-v0.4.0 the budget compares it with EDP's gain (need mass the card would resolve, sum of min(remaining, addrUse x addr)), which is in EDP's units, so EDP's number applies directly: a card resolving .06 or less of any need cannot depart however it scores (a pure synergy card on an exhausted need: EDP's 'weak departure'). The same number is the score cost of a departure; in need-mass units that bar is .06 / onRem (mean .39) = .15, close to EDP's own bar (default widgets' base .30-.45 over need widgets' .05-.20, about .3, over a median on_rem of 1.75 = .17). Cost: at slot 0 the move bar is no longer phase A's COMPOSER.moveThreshold .1, so v1 is not gam plus session machinery only; the founder's goal is EDP's behaviour (company/decisions/2026-10-20-founder-edp-faithful-personalization.md)
why.addrUse: guess: .45 (model-v0.4.1; was .35). EDP's widget addr is need mass: its 18 need widgets' primary addr has median .45 and their secondary addr median .20. Our relational addr is 1 for a primary match and .5 for a partial one, so addrUse .45 maps 1 to .45 and .5 to .225, EDP's two medians. A median repair (.41) or build (.46) need is then about used up by one primary pick, as in EDP (a .5 widget on a .5 need), and a high need (p90 .6 to .7) keeps .15 to .25, enough for a follow-on card to pass the budget. Both state vectors move by addrUse x addr (build note §8.2)

edits: guess: complementarity, EDP's chain synergies: a second successor of a recalled concept after the first (addr is fixed from history, so it is a parallel frontier step, not a successor of the first card). .28 (model-v0.4.1; was .15) = .71 x onRem.build .4: EDP's v3 synergy widgets carry on_cov at .50 to 1.43 of their own on_rem, median .71 (EDITS_V3: easy_returns_promise, style_bridge, occasion_lookbook, material_deep_dive, price_history, wishlist_save, size_guide, recently_viewed). After one addr-1 build pick (coverage .45) the term is .28 x .45 = .13: below a typical unaddressed need's primary pull (build .4 x .46 = .18, repair .5 x .41 = .21), so other needs still come first as in EDP, and above the slot-4 move bar (.06 + .01 x 4 = .10). The chain then ends where EDP's does, at the attention budget: the follow-on must still resolve more than .06 of need mass

guess: complementarity: a second lesson on a missed concept's prerequisite chain reinforces the first (repair is rarely one card). .35 (model-v0.4.1; was .15) = .71 x onRem.repair .5, the same EDP scale rule as build: .35 x .45 = .16 after one addr-1 repair pick, below a typical unaddressed primary pull and above the move bar to slot 4; the budget ends the chain
edpBaseEdits: guess: .033 (model-v0.4.3, W-2004; was the .02 placeholder), by the VP record's rule (company/decisions/2026-10-20-vp-personalization-session-base.md §2.3): beta = (EDP need-widget base spread / EDP typical primary pull) x our typical primary pull, the same statistic on both sides. EDP (orchestrator-inline.js makeModulesV1, scoreProblems on its 8 shopper profiles): base spread over the 18 need widgets = .20 - .05 = .15 (our base x rank also spans beta over the list); typical primary pull = median over the 56 persona x problem pairs of (largest primary on_rem for that problem x need) = .529; ratio .284. Ours (composition traces only, gam-session-v3, the 6 simulated learners x seeds 1-3 x 7 days, session-start needs): median over the 1,046 nonzero session x need pairs of onRem x need = .115. beta = .284 x .115 = .0326, rounded to .033. Two other matched statistics agree: median-coefficient x median-need (.15 x .1095 / .485 = .034) and each session's strongest pull (.15 x .270 / 1.168 = .035). The record's 'about .1' and 'near .02' paired EDP's strongest pull (about 1.2 to 1.5) with our median-need pull (.19), two different statistics. beta > 0 keeps the default order as the tie-break among cards with equal need terms. Not read off a layout probe or any recall field
